title: Tenant anchoring: eviction scenarios + customer comm playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working operator + comms playbook for tenant anchoring edge cases where a tenant's pinned region (anchor) is no longer available, must be moved, or has been evicted. Focus is on safe re-anchor paths, evidence for compliance/legal, customer-facing messaging, and operator scripts to minimize downtime and data-location risk.

Scope / assumptions:
- Applies to Private (VPC) and Dedicated customers with explicit region pins or contractual residency commitments.
- We assume the platform can detect anchor loss (node eviction, failed zone, lost storage attachment) and can route to fallback variants (same-region replica, geo-fallback region).
- This doc does NOT replace the primary residency enforcement policy; it is an operational addendum for edge recovery.

Quick summary for oncall:
1) Identify: telemetry alert => "anchor-loss" with tenant_id, anchor_region, evidence bucket id.
2) Assess: check contract level (SLA vs legal residency). If legal residency required, escalate to security/legal immediately.
3) Contain: disable automated cross-border failover for the tenant to avoid silent violations.
4) Remediate: run re-anchor-to-escape-region or build expedited temporary anchor (see scripts).
5) Communicate: use templates below for customer notice and internal escalation.

Signals that trigger this playbook:
- Storage volume detached or recreated in a different region for a pinned tenant.
- Sustained RPC failures to region-local endpoints (>5m) plus autoscaler moved capacity out-of-region.
- Manual anchor removal via admin console.
- Legal hold or takedown that forces migration.

Operator checklist (first 15m):
- Confirm alert details: tenant_id, pinned_region, current_routing_region, incident_id.
- Snapshot evidence: collect trace IDs, node IDs, storage object IDs, and save to evidence-bucket/tenant_id/date. (See evidence packaging conventions).
- Pull contract record: contract_residency_clause = yes/no/partial. If "yes" then set severity = P0 and notify legal.
- Toggle cross-border failover to OFF for tenant (prevent silent migration).
- If traffic still flows cross-border, add temporary rate-limit and route all new requests to a 'holding' fail endpoint that returns 503 + structured reason.

Re-anchor options (ordered by safety):
A) Local repair: restore anchor in same region. Steps:
  - If loss due to host eviction, try reattaching storage to a warm standby in same AZ.
  - If unavailable, request expedited capacity in region (dedicated customers) via reservations team.
  - Time estimate: 15–90m depending on capacity.

B) Temporary shadow anchor in adjacent compliant region with documented consent. Steps:
  - Check contract for allowed adjacent regions (some EA customers allow EU <-> EFTA but not outside).
  - Send customer opt-in template (fast path) — include explicit ETA and rollback plan.
  - Create shadow anchor, migrate least-sensitive state, route read-only until full migration is approved.
  - Time estimate: 2–8 hours (depends on customer OK).

C) Emergency cross-border fallback (last resort):
  - Only allowed for non-contractual/residency-bound tenants and with Exec-level approval for SLA-impacting actions.
  - Must be documented in evidence bundle with timestamps and justification.

Evidence collection (for compliance/legal):
- Minimum required: timestamped infra events + routing tables + storage object manifests + operator commands run.
- Preferred: signed operator runbook execution (who executed what), terminal transcript, and Slack thread link.
- Store artifacts under evidence-bundles/{tenant_id}/{incident_id}/ and produce a ZIP for legal.

Customer communication templates (copy/paste, edit as needed):
1) Initial triage notice (short):
Subject: Incident: Temporary service disruption for processed data location
Hi <CustomerName>,
We detected an infrastructure issue affecting the region where your account is pinned (<pinned_region>). We're actively investigating and have prevented any automatic cross-border routing to protect data locality. We'll follow up with the next update within 2 hours.
Regards,
Redwood Inference Support

2) Opt-in for temporary shadow anchor (requires explicit customer approval):
Subject: Request: temporary relocation window for continuity (action required)
Hi <CustomerName>,
To restore service quickly we can provision a temporary anchor in <adjacent_region> for up to <X hours>. This will allow your product to operate while we rebuild your primary anchor. This move is reversible and we will not persist long-term without your consent. Please reply with "I consent" or contact <account-rep> for questions.

3) Post-incident evidence & closure (for customers with residency clauses):
Subject: Incident closure & residency evidence bundle — <incident_id>
Hi <CustomerName>,
Attached is the evidence bundle detailing the incident, operator actions, timing, and assurance steps we took to protect data locality. We recommend a follow-up call to review mitigation and next steps for stronger anchor redundancy.

Operational scripts & snippets (pasteable):
- disable-failover-for-tenant --tenant $TENANT --incident $ID --reason "anchor-loss"
- collect-evidence --tenant $TENANT --incident $ID --out s3://evidence-bundles/$TENANT/$ID/
- create-shadow-anchor --tenant $TENANT --region $REGION --mode read-only --tag temp-eviction
- reattach-volume --volume $VOL --target-region $REGION --force-checksum-verify

QA / runbook tests to add to SRE playbook:
- Simulate host eviction with storage detach and verify alert generated + evidence bundle created.
- Simulate cross-border autoscale and verify failover toggle prevents automatic routing.
- Customer opt-in flow: mock customer reply and verify shadow anchor provisioning completes in <4h.

Edge cases & notes:
- Multi-tenant hardware: if multiple tenants pinned to same rack, ensure tenant-level evidence isolatable (no cross-tenant logs).
- Low-latency customers: shadow anchor may cause permission/latency regressions; include explicit perf tests.
- Legal holds: if a tenant is under legal hold, do NOT migrate or create shadow anchors without legal sign-off.

Open questions (items to resolve):
- What is the SLA for evidence delivery to customers after an evacuation? (Legal + PS to decide)
- Should we automate the opt-in email via Console or keep it manual for now? (UX + Security)
- What retention window for evidence bundles (security/compliance)?

Action items (owners):
- Arjun: prototype evidence bundle zipper with signature header — due 2025-02-01.
- Sofia: author the Console modal for opt-in email flow (mockups) — due 2025-02-14.
- Liam: add simulated chaos test to residency-suite (CI) and measure false-positive rate — due 2025-03-01.
- Maya: coordinate legal review for evidence SLA and add to runbook — due 2025-02-07.

Notes to self / shorthand (working):
- keep cross-border-fallback OFF by default for "pinned=true" tenants.
- build telemetry tag: residency.eviction_reason (eviction|detach|manual|legal).
- attach incident id to billing exports if SLA credit is needed.

Reference links / search terms for next iteration:
- residency evidence schema, residency.eviction telemetry, shadow-anchor API, opt-in customer template (private-deployments), legal: residency SLA clause examples.

Slack threads / trackers:
- #private-deployments (thread: anchor-loss-2025-01; pinned)
- JIRA-PRIV-8912 (reanchor API backlog)

-- end working draft --

This is intentionally informal: copy into Confluence after we've validated the scripts in staging.
